---
title: "Do high-AI-exposure majors earn higher starting salaries?"
author: "James Holdaway"
format: pdf
---

# Setup

```{r}
#| message: FALSE

library(tidyverse)

base_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/"
file_path <- "2026/2026-10-20/ai_salary_majors.csv"

ai_salary_majors <- read_csv(paste0(base_url, file_path))
```

# Exploring the data 

```{r}
glimpse(ai_salary_majors)
summary(ai_salary_majors)
```
```{r}
# finding specific majors
ai_salary_majors |>
  filter(str_detect(field_of_study, "Statistic")) |>
  select(field_of_study, median_starting_salary, ai_exposure, ai_exposure_percentile)

ai_salary_majors |>
  filter(str_detect(field_of_study, "Data Science")) |>
  select(field_of_study, median_starting_salary, ai_exposure, ai_exposure_percentile)

ai_salary_majors |>
  filter(str_detect(field_of_study, "Economic")) |>
  select(field_of_study, median_starting_salary, ai_exposure, ai_exposure_percentile)

ai_salary_majors |>
  filter(str_detect(field_of_study, "Finance")) |>
  select(field_of_study, median_starting_salary, ai_exposure, ai_exposure_percentile)

ai_salary_majors |>
  filter(str_detect(field_of_study, "Computer Science")) |>
  select(field_of_study, median_starting_salary, ai_exposure, ai_exposure_percentile)
```
```{r}
ai_salary_majors |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ai_exposure, y = median_starting_salary)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + 
  geom_smooth(method = lm) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(
    x = "AI Exposure (standardized score)",
    y = "Median Starting Salary ($)"
  )
```
